## ServiceSettings v0.3.0

Phase 2 hardening. The command layer, storage and state refresh are rebuilt on Win32 SCM and a Rust-managed JSON file; the window is frameless, with the export / import / edit controls in an in-page title bar. The Tauri 2 migration this builds on is documented in the [v0.2.0 notes](https://github.com/Jaspersol/service-settings/blob/v0.3.0/.github/release-notes/v0.2.0.md).

### Win32 SCM instead of `sc` / `net` text parsing

- The Rust command layer calls `OpenSCManagerW` → `OpenServiceW` → `QueryServiceStatusEx` / `StartServiceW` / `ControlService` directly. No `sc.exe` / `net.exe` child processes, no shell strings, no 20 s subprocess timeout.
- **GBK decoding and the `4  RUNNING` regex are gone.** Running state is read from `SERVICE_STATUS_PROCESS.dwCurrentState == SERVICE_RUNNING` (4), so `START_PENDING` / `STOP_PENDING` can never be misread.
- Win32 error codes are mapped to readable Chinese messages (5 → 拒绝访问, 1060 → 服务不存在, 1056 → 已在运行, 1062 → 未运行, 1053 → 未及时响应); anything else falls back to the system's localized `FormatMessageW` text.
- Each action requests only the access it needs: `status` uses `SERVICE_QUERY_STATUS` (elevation-free), `start` `SERVICE_START`, `stop` `SERVICE_STOP`. Service names are validated against an ASCII whitelist capped at 255 characters.
- Elevation is checked once at startup via `TokenElevation`; if UAC is declined, a **以管理员重启** button stays in the title bar so elevation can be retried without restarting the app.

### Storage: `services.json` instead of IndexedDB

- The list lives in `app_data_dir()/services.json` as an array of `{ domName, serviceName }`. **Toggle state is never persisted** — it is always read back from SCM on launch, so the file can't drift from reality.
- Writes are atomic and concurrency-safe: each save writes a **unique** temp file, `sync_all`s it and renames it into place. Two overlapping saves can no longer share one temp name and clobber each other.
- **Corrupt files are preserved**: if the JSON can't be parsed, Rust renames it to `services.json.bad-<timestamp>` and returns an error; the renderer shows a toast instead of overwriting it with placeholder data.
- **One-time migration**: if the JSON file is absent but a v0.2.x IndexedDB list (`TestDB` / `config` / id `1`) exists, `store.js` imports it, saves it to JSON and drops the old database.
- v0.1.x Electron profiles are still unreachable — those users need to re-add services or import a JSON backup.

### Periodic state refresh

- On launch the cards are wired up first and their real states are queried **in parallel**, so there is no "visible but not clickable" window while status loads.
- Every 5 seconds each card re-reads the real service state. Cards being toggled or already removed are skipped, an **in-flight guard** prevents overlapping refreshes, and refresh never writes to disk.

### Export / import

- The two buttons live in the title bar (not a bottom toolbar). Export downloads `service-settings.json` via a browser Blob (no extra Tauri permissions); the Blob URL is released only after a short delay.
- Import validates structure, field types / lengths, legal service names, duplicates, entry count and file size, then saves and reloads the page to reuse the normal startup flow.
- CSP keeps `blob:` in `default-src` so the download link can be opened.

### Window and interactions

- **Frameless window** — the borderless, fully transparent in-page title bar blends into the same gradient as the cards; the scrollbar is a low-contrast, borderless ink-grey strip.
- **Editing is explicit** — the `+` card and delete × only appear in edit mode (the 编辑 / 完成 button); the former 5000 ms hover-to-delete delay is gone.
- **Non-blocking feedback** — errors use an auto-dismissing toast and an in-page confirmation dialog instead of native `alert` / `confirm`, so the refresh timer is never stalled.
- **Empty list** — an inline hint replaces the old hard-coded `mysql` / `MySQL84` placeholder card.

### Upgrade notes

| From   | Result                                                                            |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| v0.2.x | IndexedDB list migrated to `services.json` automatically                          |
| v0.1.x | List not carried over (different runtime profile); re-add or import a JSON backup |

The identifier (`com.makabakax.service-settings`) is unchanged, as are the service-name whitelist, the `{ success, running?, message? }` response shape and the 500 ms switch debounce.

### Verification

- `cargo test --lib`: passes (injection rejection, camelCase field contract, legacy extra-field tolerance, response shape, real SCM 1060 error mapping, corrupt-config backup, status not persisted, service-name length, concurrent saves)
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npx prettier --check`: clean
- `npm run tauri build`: NSIS installer produced

### Downloads

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ServiceSettings-0.3.0-setup.exe` | NSIS installer, x64, per-user — the app relaunches itself elevated on start, so no manual "run as administrator" |

### Notes

- Windows 10/11 x64 only. The command layer uses the Win32 Service Control Manager, and the installer targets NSIS. WebView2 comes with Windows 11; on Windows 10 the installer bootstraps it.
- Reading a service's state needs no elevation; starting and stopping does. Declining the UAC prompt leaves the window usable, with a 以管理员重启 button in the title bar to retry.
- The list lives in `services.json` under Tauri's per-user app data directory. Use the title-bar export button to back it up before reinstalling; see [Upgrade notes](#upgrade-notes) for what carries over from earlier versions.
